day: Friday of week 23 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is a quiet tension in Paul's words today that speaks to something true about the spiritual life. He has bound himself freely to a task he did not choose, made himself a slave to everyone, disciplined his body like an athlete training for a prize. Yet he does not sound bitter about this surrender. Instead, he sounds alive with purpose, even peaceful. He knows what he is running toward.

The Gospel offers us the other side of this coin. While Paul describes the cost of discipleship, Jesus turns our gaze inward, reminding us that before we can guide anyone else, we must first see clearly ourselves. We become like our teacher, but only if we are honest about our own blindness, our own plank. There is no superiority here, no room for the illusion that we have already arrived. The teacher himself remains always a student, always learning, always looking at his own eye first.

Both readings ask the same gentle question: Are we willing to see ourselves truthfully, and then to give ourselves freely to something larger than ourselves? Not out of compulsion, but out of love for what we serve. Perhaps this is the peace that surpasses understanding, the dwelling place of the Lord that the psalm promises. It comes not from having all the answers, but from surrendering to the journey with open eyes.

You might pause and ask yourself today: What am I being called to serve, and what prevents me from seeing myself clearly?
